policy.text: Creating an issue requires write permission to the repository's issues unit. Read permission to the repository alone does not authorize this write.

questions.request: Does CreateIssue and its API route in this Gitea revision comply with the independently supplied current policy for authenticated repository readers and for principals with issue write permission? Trace route-level controls, repository or issue-unit checks, and the issue creation effect; identify any relevant exceptions rather than assuming endpoint-local checks are the whole authorization path, and explain policy compliance together with precise source or deployment limits.
questions.principal: authenticated repository readers and principals with issue write permission
questions.entryHint: CreateIssue and its API route in this Gitea revision

premises.text: The requested review concerns CreateIssue and its API route in this Gitea revision.

steps.name: doer
steps.claim: ctx.Doer is the principal recorded as the issue poster.

steps.name: repository
steps.claim: ctx.Repo.Repository is the repository in which the issue is requested.

steps.name: issuesUnit
steps.claim: unit.TypeIssues identifies the repository issues unit.

steps.name: repoPermission
steps.claim: ctx.Repo.Permission is the permission object used for issue-unit write checks.

steps.name: form
steps.claim: The parsed CreateIssueOption supplies title, body, deadline, milestone, assignees, labels, projects, ref, and requested closed state.

steps.name: check_deadline_issue_write
steps.claim: The handler calls CanWrite(TypeIssues) before accepting the requested deadline; this check controls the deadline field, not entry to issue creation.

steps.name: deadline_branch
steps.claim: Only an issue-unit writer's supplied deadline is copied into the new issue.

steps.name: set_deadline
steps.claim: The requested deadline is converted and assigned to the issue's DeadlineUnix field.

steps.name: continue_after_deadline
steps.claim: Continue to the common issue initialization.

steps.name: continue_without_deadline
steps.claim: Without a successful issue-write check (or without a supplied deadline), DeadlineUnix remains its zero value and processing continues.

steps.name: issue
steps.claim: The handler constructs an issue for the repository with the current doer as poster and with title, content, ref, and the conditionally accepted deadline.

steps.name: check_metadata_issue_write
steps.claim: The handler again calls CanWrite(TypeIssues) to decide whether milestone and assignee inputs may be applied; this branch does not itself decide whether an issue may be created.

steps.name: metadata_branch
steps.claim: Issue writers may supply milestone and assignees, while non-writers proceed after labels are cleared.

steps.name: set_milestone
steps.claim: For an issue-unit writer, the requested milestone is assigned to the issue.

steps.name: assignee_validation_boundary
steps.claim: Writer-supplied assignees are resolved and checked for assignability; lookup, access, or validation failures stop processing.
steps.reason: Assignee validation affects optional issue metadata and operational errors, not the shown authorization gate for the issue-creation operation itself.

steps.name: clear_labels
steps.claim: When CanWrite(TypeIssues) is false, only form.Labels is replaced by an empty list; other form fields, including title, body, projects, and the request to create an issue, are not cleared here.

steps.name: create_issue_service
steps.claim: After the non-writer branch clears labels, the handler still calls issue_service.NewIssue with the repository, issue, empty labels, no explicit attachments, assignee IDs, and requested projects.

steps.name: new_issue_result
steps.claim: A NewIssue error produces an API error and returns; a nil error means creation processing succeeded and later response processing continues.

steps.name: issue_creation_effect
steps.claim: The opaque NewIssue call has successfully performed the issue-creation operation before optional close/refetch/response processing.

steps.name: entry_success
steps.claim: Subject to later close/refetch operational success, the endpoint returns HTTP 201 with the created issue; this source alone does not establish that a non-writer was authorized because NewIssue and route middleware remain unexamined.

steps.name: new_issue_rejected
steps.claim: Blocked-user, permission/not-found, or other NewIssue errors stop the request and are mapped to API errors.
